scenes.say: An RTX 3090 has twenty-four gigabytes, and no FP8 tensor cores. Which open image and video models still fit on it?

scenes.headline: What fits in 24 GB on Ampere, and why
scenes.sub: Four open models, one brief, fixed seeds, measured
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Marisol! I gave four open models the same brief, a two-storey beach house on a beach, and timed every one of them on a 3090.

scenes.title: A weights problem
scenes.sub: What has to sit on the card, stage by stage

scenes.title: Every weight in BF16
scenes.note: PyTorch sees 23.56 GiB of the card
scenes.say: Sum every shard. The small FLUX is fourteen point eight seven gibibytes. Z-Image, nineteen point one one. The video model, twenty-three point oh eight. And Qwen-Image two point one is thirty point two one, more than the card holds.

scenes.title: Qwen-Image-2.1, one stage at a time

legend: The pipeline waits in host RAM
All of it at once: 30.21 GiB, over the card
Encode first: the text encoder alone

steps.say: Here is Qwen-Image two point one in host memory: a text encoder, a denoiser, and an autoencoder.
Put all of it on the card and it spills over the line before a single activation.

steps.term: Offload: each part on the card only while it runs
steps.say: So run one stage at a time. The text encoder comes on alone, reads the prompt once, and leaves.
Then the denoiser comes on and runs its forty steps, with plenty of room left.
The biggest part of the pipeline did its whole job in the first second. That is why offloading here is cheap.

scenes.title: What Ampere can multiply
scenes.sub: Precision is a memory lever here, not a speed lever
scenes.say: Chapter two. What Ampere can multiply.

scenes.title: Store it, or multiply in it

left.title: Tensor cores take
left.say: The 3090's tensor cores take BF16, FP16, TF32 and INT8. BF16 ran at seventy-five point five teraflops.

right.title: FP8 on the 3090
right.say: FP8 arrived a generation later. The dtype allocates, but the FP8 matmul raises an error on this card. You can store in it, not multiply in it.

scenes.title: Why smaller weights do not run faster

parts.say: Each step, every one of the small FLUX's three point eight eight billion parameters
meets each of four thousand and ninety-six image tokens,
at two FLOPs each. Thirty-one point seven teraflops, and the step took point five six five seconds.

scenes.say: That is about fifty-six teraflops, three quarters of a bare matmul. The card is already busy. Fewer bits cannot make it faster.

steps.say: The small FLUX in BF16, seed eleven: two point six seconds.
The same seed with the denoiser stored in FP8. Three point six gibibytes less, five percent slower, and the chimney moved.
And at two thousand and forty-eight pixels, eighteen point six seconds, with four hundred and eighty-two mebibytes left on the board.

scenes.title: Five seconds of it moving
scenes.sub: Kandinsky 6.0 Lite distill, from the best still
scenes.say: Chapter three. Five seconds of it moving.

steps.say: Start from the small FLUX's golden-hour still, fifteen thirty-six by eight sixty-four.
The video model resizes it to its own frame, eight sixty-four by four eighty.

steps.term: visual_cond_scheme: how the reference image enters
steps.say: This is the setting that matters. With the default scheme, the clip forgot the image after one noisy frame. Tail conditioning keeps it.
Ten steps at thirteen point seven eight seconds each, with module offload holding forty-seven point three gibibytes of host memory.
A hundred and twenty-one frames. Three minutes fifty-one seconds, load included.
And here it is. The shingles, the balcony and the boardwalk hold while the camera moves in.

scenes.title: What broke
scenes.say: Here is what broke, and each one is fixable.

items.text: Image to video ignored the image
items.say: Image to video ignored the image, even the repository's own example, on the default conditioning scheme. Tail conditioning fixed it for my stills.
Z-Image finished all nine steps at two thousand and forty-eight pixels, then ran out of memory in the decoder.
And the FP8 matmul simply refused to run on compute capability eight point six.

scenes.text: On a 3090, precision buys memory, never speed. If the BF16 weights fit, run BF16; if not, offload by stage.
scenes.say: On a 3090, precision buys memory, never speed. If the BF16 weights fit, run them in BF16. If they don't, offload one stage at a time.

recap: FP8 is storage only on Ampere
Kandinsky needs tail conditioning for stills
scenes.say: To recap. The small FLUX makes an image in two point six seconds. FP8 is only storage on Ampere. And the video model needs tail conditioning to keep your still.
